correctness.rationale: At a P-point, every continuous f is locally constant at p because all countably many inverse-image neighborhoods of f(p) intersect in the level set, itself a neighborhood. Approximate positive norming f_n with f_n(p)=1 are identically 1 on common neighborhood W; choose a nonnegative continuous bump g<=f_n everywhere with g(p)=1 by compact Hausdorff normality. Norm monotonicity gives ||g||<=1 and evaluation gives >=1. At non-P-point, choose open U_n with intersection not a neighborhood, F_n=K\U_n; ||f||*=||f||inf+sum 2^-n||f|F_n||inf is an equivalent lattice norm. Bumps supported in finite intersections show ||delta_p||*=1, while any f(p)=1 is nonzero on some F_n and must cost >1. No sequence convergence or metrizability used; no numerical calculation substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: An exact topological iff criterion for universal evaluation norm attainment across every equivalent lattice renorming naturally organizes the apparently exceptional ordinal example and produces a constructive counterexample for every non-P point, including nonsequential spaces. This is a structural classification with genuinely broader hypotheses.

final_claim: For compact Hausdorff K and p in K, evaluation delta_p on real C(K) attains its dual norm under every equivalent lattice norm iff p is a P-point (countable intersections of neighborhoods remain neighborhoods). At a non-P point an explicit weighted restriction renorming makes delta_p norm-one but nonattaining.
